### [1] [TransBiolab: A Real-World Multi-View Dataset of Cluttered Transparent Biomedical Objects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21071)
*Ke Ma,Yifei Wang,Meng Wang,Tian Xia*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TransBiolab is a real-world RGB-D dataset of 161,315 frames from 98 cluttered transparent biomedical object scenes, featuring 1.03M instance annotations across 15 object types with 6D poses, masks, depth, and multi-view calibration, designed to benchmark segmentation, depth estimation, 6D pose estimation, and robot manipulation in autonomous lab settings.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing transparent-object datasets lack evaluation in the combined setting of multi-object clutter, occlusion, and calibrated multi-view capture characteristic of real laboratory manipulation scenes, limiting progress in autonomous biomedical laboratories that rely on visual perception of transparent plasticware.

Method: The authors constructed TransBiolab by capturing 98 scenes of cluttered transparent biomedical objects as calibrated multi-view RGB-D sequences, annotating 1.03M instances with 6D poses, full/visible masks, depth, and per-frame camera calibration, and organizing the data along three difficulty axes: object category, object count, and camera viewpoint.

Result: The dataset contains 161,315 frames across 98 scenes covering 15 laboratory object types, with dataset-centric benchmarks defined for segmentation, depth estimation/completion, and 6D pose estimation, plus a system-level robot manipulation evaluation.

Conclusion: TransBiolab addresses the gap in domain-relevant transparent-object data for autonomous biomedical manipulation by providing richly annotated multi-view sequences in cluttered settings, serving as a resource for advancing segmentation, depth estimation, 6D pose estimation, and multi-view reasoning in real laboratory environments.

Abstract: Autonomous biomedical laboratories increasingly rely on visual perception to recognize, localize, and manipulate transparent plasticware, yet high-quality real-world datasets for this setting remain limited. The scarcity of domain-relevant data is particularly restrictive in cluttered multi-object scenes, where mutual occlusion and view-dependent appearance changes remain challenging even for contemporary visual foundation models. Existing transparent-object datasets have advanced segmentation, depth, and pose estimation, but they usually do not evaluate the combined setting of multi-object clutter, occlusion, and calibrated multi-view capture that characterizes real laboratory manipulation scenes. To address this gap, we present TrainsBiolab, a real-world RGB-D dataset of cluttered transparent biomedical objects captured as calibrated multi-view sequences. TrainsBiolab contains 161,315 frames from 98 scenes and 1.03M instance annotations over 15 laboratory object types, including 6D poses, full and visible masks, depth, and per-frame camera calibration. The dataset is organized along three axes that reflect operational difficulty: object category, the total number of objects in a frame, and camera viewpoint. We further define dataset-centric benchmarks for segmentation, depth estimation and completion, and 6D pose estimation, and report a system-level robot manipulation evaluation enabled by the released annotations and calibrations. By focusing on repeated transparent instances, clutter, and multi-view laboratory capture, TrainsBiolab provides a resource for segmentation, depth estimation, 6D pose estimation, and multi-view reasoning in autonomous laboratory manipulation. Project page: https://dualtransparency.github.io/TransBiolab/.

</details>


### [2] [3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20789)
*Xuening Tian,Dieter Schmalstieg,Shohei Mori*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: 3D-GIMP proposes a hybrid paradigm for object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting that performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, then uses a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate textures across remaining views, avoiding computationally expensive multi-view diffusion and hallucination drift.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing 3D scene editing methods using iterative diffusion models are computationally expensive, struggle to produce sharp details, and suffer from "hallucination drift" causing multi-view inconsistencies and structural artifacts in novel view rendering.

Method: 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view as an appearance prior, then applies a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, bypassing frame-by-frame diffusion.

Result: 3D-GIMP achieves competitive inpainting quality compared to multi-view diffusion methods, while outperforming them in rendering speed and view consistency, maintaining high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions.

Conclusion: Prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation via single-view inpainting + correspondence propagation yields mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction with superior efficiency and consistency.

Abstract: Recent advances in 3D scene editing have leveraged iterative diffusion models to update input views. However, this process is computationally expensive and struggles to produce sharp details. Meanwhile, ``hallucination drift'' frequently introduces multi-view inconsistencies, leading to structural artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints. To address this problem, we present 3D-GIMP (3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets Patch Matching), a novel hybrid paradigm designed for high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of diffusing every view, 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, which serves as an appearance prior. We then introduce a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate these reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, effectively bypassing the stochastic nature of frame-by-frame diffusion. By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP maintains high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions while ensuring a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction. Our experiments demonstrate that 3D-GIMP not only achieves competitive inpainting quality as previous methods using diffusion in multiple views, but also outperforms these methods in rendering speed and view consistency.

</details>


### [3] [Learning-based Seam Correspondence Reconstruction in Sewing Patterns](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21213)
*Zhendong Wang,Jintong Wang,Chen Liu,Yao Jin,Ligang Liu,Huamin Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A graph-based learning framework reconstructs coarse panel connectivity and fine-grained seam correspondences from 2D sewing pattern geometry without manual annotations, supporting complex topologies like curved seams and many-to-one correspondences.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Digital sewing patterns lack explicit stitch annotations, making downstream 3D modeling reliant on labor-intensive expert specification. The goal is to automate stitching reconstruction from 2D panel geometry alone.

Method: A two-level graph-based framework: (1) Coarse level infers panel connectivity by predicting panel semantics tied to anatomical body regions; (2) Fine-grained level infers seam correspondences between panel pairs via latent edge representations learned through graph message passing that encode local seam geometry and global garment context.

Result: High stitching accuracy and strong generalization across diverse garment styles, handling complex topologies such as many-to-one correspondences, intra-panel seams, and curved seams.

Conclusion: The proposed method effectively automates stitching reconstruction from raw 2D panels, reducing reliance on manual annotation for downstream 3D garment modeling.

Abstract: Digital sewing patterns typically consist of disjoint 2D panels without explicit stitch annotations, making downstream 3D modeling reliant on labor-intensive expert specification. In this paper, we present a graph-based learning framework that reconstructs two-level stitching information, coarse panel connectivity and fine-grained seam correspondence, from 2D panel geometry alone. At the coarse level, panel connectivity is inferred by predicting panel semantics associated with anatomical body regions, enforcing consistency with body structure and garment design conventions. Based on the reconstructed panel graph, fine-grained seam correspondences between panel pairs are inferred by learning latent edge representations that jointly encode local seam geometry and global garment context through graph message passing. The resulting edge embeddings are subsequently decoded into detailed seam correspondences. Our method supports complex sewing-pattern topologies, including many-to-one correspondences, intra-panel seams, and curved seams. Experiments demonstrate high stitching accuracy and strong generalization across garment styles.

</details>


### [4] [Scene Parameter Saliency via Differentiable Light Transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21562)
*Linas Beresna,Eugene Fiume*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Differentiable renderers can generate metric saliency maps via reverse-mode differentiation, propagating attribution through the image formation process to reveal which scene parameters most influence any scalar image metric, analogous to gradient-based saliency in neural networks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To extend the concept of gradient-based saliency from neural network interpretability to physically-based image formation, enabling scene understanding through differentiated rendering rather than learned weights.

Method: Apply reverse-mode differentiation through differentiable renderers to compute per-parameter gradients for any scalar metric evaluated on a rendered image, producing metric saliency maps across different objectives (glare indices, luminance, perceptual scores).

Result: Metric saliency rankings differ substantially across objectives for the same scene; parameters dominating one metric may be negligible for another, demonstrating saliency is metric-specific rather than an intrinsic scene property.

Conclusion: Derivative images from differentiable renderers are as informative for scene understanding as the primal rendered images, providing a new tool for analyzing parameter influence in image formation.

Abstract: Gradient-based saliency methods reveal which input features most influence a neural network's output, and are a standard tool for model interpretability. We observe that differentiable renderers, which are conventionally used for parameter optimisation, produce an analogous form of saliency: given any scalar metric evaluated on a rendered image, a single reverse-mode differentiation pass yields per-parameter gradients that identify which scene elements most influence the metric. We call these gradient fields metric saliency maps. Unlike neural saliency, which propagates attribution through learned weights, metric saliency propagates through the image formation process itself, including multi-bounce light transport, capturing parameter dependencies that are semi-opaque to manual inspection. We compute metric saliency maps for qualitatively different objectives: psychovisual glare indices, mean scene luminance, and neural perceptual scores. The saliency rankings differ substantially across metrics for the same scene, with parameters that dominate one objective being negligible for another. The saliency map is specific to the metric, not an intrinsic property of the scene. Our results suggest that differentiable renderers produce derivative images that are as informative for scene understanding as the primal images they were designed to generate.

</details>


### [5] [RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20628)
*Renbiao Jin,Mingxin Yang,Yutian Chen,Junhao Zhuang,Xin Cai,Mulin Yu,Linning Xu,Wenxian Yu,Danping Zou,Shi Guo,Tianfan Xue*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RealVDeblur is an efficient generative framework for real-world video deblurring that uses a physically grounded 3D Gaussian Splatting blur synthesis pipeline, a video diffusion prior with frame-wise VAE encoding, and distills multi-step diffusion into a one-step generator with a training-free Temporal Window Mask for long-video inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world video deblurring is challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream tasks like mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction.

Method: (1) Large-scale physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline using 3D Gaussian Splatting assets and high-frame-rate videos. (2) Video diffusion prior with disabled temporal VAE compression and frame-wise encoding for better blur variation handling. (3) Distillation of multi-step diffusion into one-step generator, plus training-free Temporal Window Mask for long-video inference with constant memory.

Result: Strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos; improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur.

Conclusion: RealVDeblur achieves robust in-the-wild video deblurring with efficient deployment on long videos, validated across diverse real-world benchmarks.

Abstract: Real-world video deblurring remains challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and the scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream pipelines such as mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction. This work presents \textbf{RealVDeblur}, an efficient generative framework designed to improve in-the-wild robustness under diverse real capture conditions. First, a large-scale, physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline is constructed from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos, providing realistic training data covering both camera-induced and object-motion blur. Second, a video diffusion prior is leveraged for restoration; to better accommodate frame-dependent blur variations, temporal compression in the VAE is disabled and a frame-wise encoding scheme is adopted. For practical deployment on long videos, multi-step diffusion sampling is distilled into an efficient one-step generator, and a training-free Temporal Window Mask stabilizes inference beyond the training horizon with constant memory usage. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, as well as improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur. Project page: https://rbjin.github.io/RealVDeblur

</details>


### [6] [Masked Topology Modeling for Self-Supervised Learning on Parametric CAD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20642)
*Heinrich Jiang,Jennifer Jang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper proposes Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), a self-supervised pretraining method for CAD B-Rep data that masks edges in face-adjacency graphs and predicts masked edge properties, combined with contrastive learning and masked reconstruction, achieving strong benchmark performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: CAD is ubiquitous but there is a shortage of editable parametric B-Rep datasets, motivating the need for data-efficient methods in this domain.

Method: A self-supervised pretraining task called Masked Topology Modeling (MTM) that masks edges in the face-adjacency graph of B-Reps and trains a head to predict masked edge convexity and curve type from post-message-passing face features, combined with MoCo-style contrastive learning over B-Rep-aware augmentations and BFS-connected face-region masked reconstruction, pretrained on ABC and a new procedurally generated dataset.

Result: Strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

Conclusion: MTM and the combined pretraining approach are effective for learning representations from limited B-Rep data, demonstrated by strong benchmark results.

Abstract: Computer aided design (CAD) is ubiquitous: virtually any modern object was designed using editable CAD tools. However, with the shortage of available CAD datasets in its native editable and parametric format, boundary representation (B-Rep), it is ever more important to develop data-efficient methods for this domain.
  We present a new self-supervised pretraining task, Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), that leverages the face-adjacency graph, an induced structure unique to B-reps that the encoder can be asked to reconstruct. MTM masks a fraction of edges and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from the encoder's post-message-passing face features.
  We combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations, a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective, and pretraining on the ABC dataset and our new procedurally generated dataset to show strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

</details>


### [7] [Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20660)
*Anita Hu,Maria Shugrina*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Axolotl3D is a unified multi-modal, occlusion-aware 3D generation model that conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and partial point clouds to achieve controllable 3D completion across diverse inputs, achieving SOTA on Toys4K and OmniObject3D.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing 3D generative models assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Prior works address these issues individually but lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals.

Method: Axolotl3D jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud acts as a geometric anchor for faithful shape completion, camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment, and a unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data for robust cross-modal reasoning.

Result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Toys4K and OmniObject3D under both clean and occluded settings, with strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

Conclusion: Axolotl3D provides a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals, excelling across clean, occluded, real-world, and editing scenarios.

Abstract: Recent 3D generative models produce high-quality geometry from a single image using large-scale priors and diffusion architectures. However, they assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Although prior works address these challenges individually, they lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals. We present Axolotl3D, a multi-modal and occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor promoting faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data, enabling robust cross-modal reasoning. Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, as well as strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

</details>


### [8] [ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20670)
*Yordanka Velikova,Mahdi Saleh,Liming Kuang,Benjamin Busam*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ODeform extends Neural ODEs to model continuous 4D deformation dynamics of deformable objects from 3D point clouds and physical conditions, achieving efficient, accurate motion prediction without discrete time steps.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing deformation modeling methods rely on either learning-based approaches with discrete time steps or computationally intensive physics simulators, lacking both continuity and real-time efficiency for tasks like manipulation and simulation.

Method: ODeform maps 3D point clouds and physical conditions (e.g., material properties) into a unified latent space, then solves Neural ODEs over time to model deformation as continuous flows within this embedding, eliminating discrete time step constraints.

Result: Outperforms baseline methods in motion prediction accuracy on unseen physical parameter configurations, with successful transfer to real 3D captured objects of novel shapes and effective interpolation/extrapolation of learned dynamics.

Conclusion: Neural ODE-based continuous deformation modeling offers a computationally efficient and accurate alternative for real-time deformable object modeling, with strong generalization to unseen parameters and real-world shapes.

Abstract: Modeling continuous object deformation is important for many computer vision and robotics tasks, such as manipulation and simulation. Existing approaches rely on learning-based methods or physics simulators to model shape deformations. However, these approaches either use discrete time steps or are too computationally intensive for real-time applications. We present ODeform, a novel extension of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space. Our method transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions (like material properties) into a unified latent space. By solving the resulting ordinary differential equations over time, we model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating the need for discrete time steps while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on unseen physical parameter configurations, showing improved motion prediction accuracy over baseline methods. Our experiments further demonstrate a successful transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes, along with effective interpolation and extrapolation of the learned dynamics. Our code and data will be made publicly available.

</details>


### [9] [Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20691)
*Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy,Dunren Che,Haitham Y. Adarbah,Afzel Noore*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SG-CBM uses coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to improve spatial faithfulness of concept explanations in medical imaging, achieving better diagnostic and concept performance on breast ultrasound.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Standard Concept Bottleneck Models in medical imaging suffer from spatially unfaithful explanations, where predicted concept activations are driven by irrelevant anatomical regions rather than meaningful lesion areas, limiting trustworthiness.

Method: SG-CBM incorporates coarse lesion masks to define two clinically motivated zones (in-lesion ROI for morphology, posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena) and trains concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective, using a linear bottleneck classifier to preserve semantic faithfulness.

Result: Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. A Train-corrupt/Test-clean stress test quantifies the impact of supervision quality.

Conclusion: Data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation are essential for deployable healthcare AI systems.

Abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models provide interpretable-by-design predictions by mediating diagnosis through human-understandable concepts, but in medical imaging, their trustworthiness is often limited by the quality and granularity of available supervision. In particular, predicted concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, leading to spatially unfaithful explanations. We study a data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) that leverages coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to encourage anatomically plausible concept evidence. For breast ultrasound, we derive two clinically motivated zones from each lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion region of interest for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. We train concept maps using a grouped spatial grounding objective and preserve semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the proposed SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. We also perform a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to quantify the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness. Overall, the results underscore the need for data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation for deployable healthcare AI systems.

</details>


### [10] [DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20692)
*Eric Regina,Richard Arnaud,Samir Hadi Cisneros*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation using Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching combined with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline. The best model achieves a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and FID of 0.3290, but geometric filtering, while reducing memorization and membership inference, cannot fully eliminate deeper patient-specific anatomical identity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To develop a privacy-preserving method for generating synthetic lung CT slices that balances visual realism with protection against patient re-identification and memorization of training data.

Method: Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training, plus a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning to filter generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces.

Result: Best model achieved a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and FID of 0.3290. Geometric filtering reduced nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage.

Conclusion: Preventing direct image copying is insufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity; persistent patient re-identification scores reveal a remaining privacy frontier for medical image generation.

Abstract: We present a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge. The approach combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline that filters generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning. Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off, with the best-performing model achieving a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and competitive visual fidelity with an FID of 0.3290. While the proposed geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, highlighting an important frontier for future privacy-preserving medical image generation.

</details>


### [11] [U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20705)
*Elijah Danquah Darko,Min Xian,Terence Soule,Tiankai Yao,Matthew William Anderson*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: U-CFR is an inference-time framework that uses boundary-aware uncertainty scores to generate internal pseudo-clicks for self-correction in interactive image segmentation, improving click efficiency and boundary accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing interactive image segmentation methods require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly, making image annotation inefficient.

Method: U-CFR introduces (1) a boundary-aware uncertainty score fusing segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and edge predictions to guide pseudo-click placement; (2) a dual-head network (segmentation head + edge head) with a shared encoder-decoder backbone; and (3) a cascade of refinement steps where each stage uses uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to progressively refine the mask.

Result: U-CFR reduces required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley, and improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy.

Conclusion: U-CFR offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation framework by enabling models to autonomously self-correct without additional manual input.

Abstract: Interactive image segmentation is critical for efficient image annotation; however, existing methods often require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly. We propose Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR), a novel inference-time framework that enables models to autonomously self-correct after each user interaction. U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to guide the placement of internal pseudo-clicks. These self-generated clicks target the most ambiguous boundary regions, providing strong corrective signals without additional manual input. To support this process, we design a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder backbone: a segmentation head ensures region consistency, while an edge head sharpens boundary alignment. In inference, U-CFR launches a cascade of refinement steps, where each stage leverages the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to refine the mask progressively. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed U-CFR improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy. It reduces the required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley and offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

</details>


### [12] [Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20780)
*Inpyo Song,Jangwon Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Current OWVAD evaluation suffers from "definition blindness" where models appear strong by primarily detecting normal vs. target anomalies, while being insensitive to the queried definition. The paper diagnoses this via metric decomposition, proposes three new definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ), and introduces DeCoS scoring that improves definition following by 7.3-28.3 AUROC points.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing OWVAD evaluations fail to isolate definition-conditioned behavior; they are dominated by target-vs-normal separation (7.2-26.8× more weight), allowing models to achieve strong scores while ignoring the queried definition of abnormality.

Method: (1) Decomposed dynamic-definition evaluation into target-vs-normal detection and target-vs-other-anomaly discrimination to diagnose definition blindness. (2) Introduced three progressive metrics: DC-Disc (remove normal-frame shortcut), DC-DetΔ (remove generic-anomaly shortcut), DC-SelΔ (remove multi-event selection shortcut). (3) Proposed DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions.

Result: Strong VAD, OWVAD, and vision-language baselines show weak definition following with near-zero margins. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 on DC-DetΔ across UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD.

Conclusion: OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring rather than anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

Abstract: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) is expected to detect events that match a user-specified definition of abnormality. This requirement is stronger than generic anomaly localization: in the same video, changing the definition should change which temporal regions are scored as anomalous. We show that current OWVAD evaluation largely fails to isolate this conditional behavior. Standard VAD metrics and the dynamic-definition protocol can be dominated by target-versus-normal separation, allowing models to obtain strong scores while remaining nearly insensitive to the queried definition. We call this failure mode definition blindness. To explain why it is missed, we decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination, and find that the former receives 7.2-26.8$\times$ more weight across common VAD benchmarks. Motivated by this diagnosis, we introduce three definition-conditioned evaluation metrics, DC-Disc, DC-Det$Δ$, and DC-Sel$Δ$, which progressively remove normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection shortcuts. Experiments on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD reveal that several strong VAD, OWVAD, and general vision language model baselines localize anomalous moments but exhibit weak definition following, often with near-zero definition-response margins. To validate that the failure is actionable, we further introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC points on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 points on DC-Det$Δ$. Overall, our results argue that OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

</details>


### [13] [Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20790)
*Husanpreet Singh,Robert Tran,Ayushree Kharel,Sudipta Banerjee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper evaluates iris quality metrics on VR headset data, addresses VR-specific challenges (off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, specular reflection) using generative models, and performs unimodal and multimodal (iris + periocular) recognition, finding that multimodal fusion reduces EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Traditional iris recognition protocols may be inadequate for unconstrained acquisition typical of VR-based data, necessitating evaluation and adaptation of biometric methods for VR headsets.

Method: Evaluates ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on the VRBiom dataset; addresses VR-specific challenges (off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, specular reflection) using generative models; performs unimodal (iris, periocular) and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular) recognition.

Result: Some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition; multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition.

Conclusion: Current iris quality metrics have limitations on VR data, generative model-based image adjustments improve periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion significantly enhances recognition performance. Evaluation scripts will be released for reproducibility.

Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) headsets (e.g., Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro) provide a seamless user experience due to their fast, frictionless interaction with the physical world in a simulated environment. User authentication relies on biometric cues such as iris in such headsets. However, traditional iris recognition protocols may not be adequate in cases of unconstrained acquisition, which is typical of VR-based data. In this work, we examine three crucial aspects: (1) evaluating ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset and analyzing their limitations, (2) addressing data-specific challenges such as off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection using generative models, and (3) performing unimodal (iris, periocular) recognition and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular). We observe that some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; whereas, image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition performance. We will release the evaluation scripts upon acceptance for reproducibility.

</details>


### [14] [SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20813)
*Jiun Lee,Jaekwang Kim,Sangmin Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SubSplat introduces a Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) that subdivides primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives from low-resolution features, resolving the trade-off between rendering detail and computational cost in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting for efficient, high-fidelity novel-view synthesis.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: High-resolution novel-view synthesis with pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting faces a critical trade-off: increasing input resolution improves detail but quadratically raises network cost, while low-resolution inputs stabilize cost but produce insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts.

Method: SubSplat proposes Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) that subdivides primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives to restore structural density directly from low-resolution features, enhanced by feature aggregation across multiple views to capture high-frequency details.

Result: Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID show SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency, successfully resolving the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost.

Conclusion: The proposed framework effectively resolves the inherent trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and computational cost in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting, enabling efficient high-quality rendering from low-resolution inputs.

Abstract: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting enables efficient and generalizable novel-view synthesis. However, high-resolution rendering faces a critical trade-off where increasing input resolution improves detail at the expense of quadratically rising network computational cost. Conversely, maintaining low-resolution inputs stabilizes this cost but results in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. To address this, we propose SubSplat, which introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer(SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density directly from low-resolution features. We further enhance the reparameterization quality through feature aggregation, which effectively captures high-frequency details across multiple views. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency. Our results validate that the proposed framework successfully resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting.

</details>


### [15] [Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20819)
*Thomas Kassiotis,Stefanos Gkikas,Nikolaos Smyrnis,Giorgos Giannakakis*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: StressGAT is a Graph Attention Network that uses Differential Action Units and Multiple Instance Learning to achieve 88.62% accuracy in personalized stress recognition from facial dynamics, while providing interpretability through peak stress interval identification and expressivity phenotyping.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Traditional RNNs and CNNs overlook person-specific baselines, lack capacity to model non-linear temporal distress progression, and lack interpretability required for clinical deployment.

Method: Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Differential Action Units (normalizing responses relative to neutral baselines) and Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism for interpretability; evaluated via Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation on 58 participants.

Result: Achieves 88.62% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort using subject-independent LOSO cross-validation.

Conclusion: StressGAT provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring by simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability.

Abstract: Stress is a dynamic process characterized by significant individual variability in facial expression. Traditional architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often overlook person-specific baselines or lack the representational capacity to model the non-linear temporal progression of distress due to sequential bottlenecks and rigid grid-based constraints. Furthermore, many deep learning models lack the interpretability required for clinical deployment. This study introduces StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages the relational inductive bias of graph modeling to capture complex facial dynamics that indicate acute stress. By using Differential Action Units, the framework normalizes individual responses relative to neutral baselines to achieve personalized recognition. The proposed model achieves 88.62\% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort (58 participants) using a subject-independent, Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation protocol. Beyond predictive accuracy, the architecture integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal distinct expressivity phenotypes. By simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability, this framework provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring.

</details>


### [16] [Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20866)
*Zhijing Yang,Haocheng Lin,Zhihua Xu,Haojie Li,Keze Wang,Liang Lin,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Agentic Designer is a multi-agent framework for generating interior furniture layouts that explicitly verifies geometric constraints at each step via a Generator-Evaluator-Refiner pipeline, outperforming existing one-shot methods. It also introduces InStruct, a benchmark with 18,000+ annotated samples and structure-centric metrics.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing one-shot generation methods (diffusion models, LLMs) lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, leading to structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints (walls, doors, windows).

Method: A progressive multi-agent framework (Agentic Designer) with three specialized agents—Generator, Evaluator, and Refiner—coordinated by a Progressive Consensus Mechanism that performs stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, decomposing layout synthesis into modular proposal, verification, and adjustment stages.

Result: Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

Conclusion: Progressive, constraint-verified multi-agent frameworks are superior to one-shot generation paradigms for structure-aware interior layout design, effectively preventing error accumulation through iterative geometric validation.

Abstract: Generating realistic interior furniture layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints (e.g., walls, doors, and windows) remains a fundamental challenge in automated spatial design. Existing approaches, primarily based on one-shot generation using diffusion models or Large Language Models (LLMs), lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, often resulting in structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints. To address these challenges, we propose Agentic Designer, a progressive, multi-agent framework that formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative and constraint-verified decision process. By decomposing layout synthesis into modular stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, the framework coordinates three specialized agents, a Generator, an Evaluator, and a Refiner, through a Progressive Consensus Mechanism. This mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, thereby preventing error accumulation. To facilitate this structure-aware paradigm and standardize evaluation, we establish InStruct, a comprehensive benchmark that integrates a dataset comprising over 18,000 high-quality, parametrically annotated samples with a novel suite of structure-centric metrics. Extensive quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies show that Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

</details>


### [17] [ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20868)
*Han Li,Si Liu,Zehao Huang,Dongxin Lyu,Longfei Xu,Jiahui Fu,Daxin Tian,Yuliang Xiu,Naiyan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ViSTR-Bench is a new benchmark evaluating whether MLLMs can perform qualitative spatial-temporal reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes, revealing that current models significantly underperform humans.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing MLLMs struggle with fundamental spatial-temporal abilities that humans naturally develop. Current benchmarks focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues underexplored.

Method: ViSTR-Bench is designed with principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation. It includes four evaluation dimensions (Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, Physical Dynamics), 15 subtasks, and 1,340 video QA pairs spanning tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios.

Result: Extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs shows they still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

Conclusion: Current MLLMs have strong general video understanding but lack robust spatial-temporal reasoning, highlighting a critical gap that ViSTR-Bench can systematically expose and guide future improvements.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse expert-level tasks, but they still struggle with fundamental abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous observation of the real world, such as spatial perception and dynamic reasoning. Recent studies have recognized this gap and introduced dedicated benchmarks to evaluate the spatial-temporal capabilities of MLLMs. However, existing benchmarks mostly focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues largely underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Visual Spatial-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark (ViSTR-Bench), a novel evaluation suite designed to systematically assess whether MLLMs can perform qualitative reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes. Guided by the principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation, ViSTR-Bench establishes a comprehensive four-dimensional evaluations covering Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics. The benchmark comprises 15 distinct subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video question-answer pairs spanning diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios. Extensive evaluations of a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs reveal that, despite their strong general video understanding capabilities, current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

</details>


### [18] [Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20874)
*Zhihua Xu,Zhijing Yang,Yufeng Yang,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper introduces a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR) with two datasets (Web-COCO and Web-Pascal) and proposes a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework that learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations to handle noisy labels, achieving superior results over baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Webly supervised learning is underexplored for multi-label recognition due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols, despite its potential to reduce reliance on costly manual annotations.

Method: The authors construct a WS-MLR benchmark (Web-COCO, Web-Pascal) using ~300k web images, and propose DBMLCL — a dual-branch contrastive learning framework that jointly learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations along with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels.

Result: DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines on the constructed benchmark under a unified evaluation setting.

Conclusion: The benchmark and DBMLCL framework effectively advance webly supervised multi-label recognition, addressing the gap in unified evaluation for this task.

Abstract: Training deep learning models with freely available web images can reduce their dependence on costly manual annotations. Although webly supervised learning has been widely studied for single-label recognition, its multi-label counterpart remains underexplored, partly due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols. To address this gap, we construct a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR), including Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting. The two datasets cover the same 80 and 20 categories as MS-COCO and Pascal VOC, respectively, and contain about 300 thousand images retrieved from the Internet using category-word combinations as search keywords. We further propose a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework, which learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations together with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels. Extensive experiments on the benchmark demonstrate that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines.

</details>


### [19] [WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20883)
*Ming Hu,Mingyu Dou,Jianfu Yin,Miaomiao Zhang,Cong Hu,Yao Wang,Bingliang Hu,Quan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: WhereEdit is a one-step text-to-image editing framework that introduces explicit spatial control by automatically identifying editable regions from internal model features and applying adaptive local modulation, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining one-step efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing one-step T2I editing methods lack explicit spatial control over where to edit and struggle to achieve strong semantic modifications within target regions under the one-step setting due to global semantic transport.

Method: WhereEdit reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing by automatically identifying semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applying adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency.

Result: WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods on the PIE-Bench benchmark, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining one-step generation efficiency.

Conclusion: Explicit spatial reasoning is crucial for high-quality one-step image editing, and WhereEdit demonstrates that localized adaptive editing can effectively address the limitations of global semantic transport in one-step settings.

Abstract: Recent one-step text-to-image (T2I) models enable efficient image synthesis and provide new opportunities for real-time image editing. However, existing one-step editing methods primarily rely on text conditioning for semantic transformation, lacking explicit spatial control over \textit{where} to edit. More importantly, even when spatial constraints are introduced, these methods often struggle to achieve strong and stable semantic modifications within the target regions. In this work, we revisit one-step image editing from a spatially controlled perspective and identify two key challenges: discovering editable regions and achieving effective localized semantic transformation. We reveal that existing methods perform global semantic transport, which limits high-intensity local editing under the one-step setting. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{WhereEdit}, a framework that reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing. WhereEdit automatically identifies semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency. Experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark demonstrate that WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining the efficiency of one-step generation. Additional experiments with region-level supervision further highlight the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step image editing.

</details>


### [20] [Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20889)
*Junhao Chen,Xinghao Chen,Henghaofan Zhang,Zihao Qiao,Saining Zhang,Yongzhi Li,Ruqi Huang,Sisi Li,Yimin Sheng,Jianyi Zhu,Hao Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Lumera is a benchmark and pipeline for parsing light-aware, engine-native 3D scenes from single images, using 2,513 UE5 projects with 3.73M components and 102.6K parametric lights. Lumera-Box achieves the best detection/layout scores, while Lumera-Light recovers nearly all scenes (recall 0.998) but struggles with individual-light localization (F1 0.209).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing single-image 3D scene methods produce room-scale geometry with baked/global illumination, lacking object instances and parametric lights that are editable, movable, and importable into standard game engines.

Method: Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt a VLM to parse object bounding boxes and parametric light tuples (position, color, intensity) from a single image. These are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop, trained on the Lumera-2K dataset (2,513 UE5 projects).

Result: Lumera-Box achieves merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762, outperforming DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D on overall detection/geometry/semantic/layout. Lumera-Light achieves 0.998 recall but F1 0.209 at 0.5m, with median position error 0.261m, ΔE2000 4.59, intensity Pearson r=0.628.

Conclusion: Parametric lights are established as a measurable editable-scene target. Remaining bottlenecks include relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

Abstract: Editable 3D scene creation requires object instances and lights that can be inspected, moved, and imported into standard engines, yet existing single-image methods largely stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation. We introduce Lumera (Light-aware Unified Engine-native Reconstruction and Assembly), a benchmark and reference pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing from a single image. Lumera-2K is built from 2,513 UE5 projects and provides 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views. On this data, Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I), which are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. In a sanitized box benchmark against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D, Lumera-Box obtains the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762), while WildDet3D remains stronger on anchor recall. For lights, Lumera-Light recovers almost all non-empty scenes (recall 0.998) but remains limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, and intensity Pearson r=0.628. These results establish parametric lights as a measurable editable-scene target and expose remaining bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

</details>


### [21] [MAGE-Vein: Multi-Instance Age and Gender Estimation from Finger Vein Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20897)
*Katsuki Tanaka,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki,Masakazu Fujio,Yosuke Kaga,Kanade Oshima,Kenta Takahashi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MAGE-Vein is a multi-instance, multi-task learning framework for age estimation from finger vein images that uses three-finger fusion and simultaneous gender classification to overcome demographic biases and confounding factors, achieving MAE of 6.12 years and correlation of 0.880, demonstrating that previous failures were due to biased datasets rather than modality limitations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Age estimation from finger vein images was previously deemed impractical due to demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors such as gender.

Method: Proposes MAGE-Vein, a multi-instance, multi-task learning framework with hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers to extract robust aging signs and suppress local noise, with simultaneous gender classification to eliminate gender-specific vascular variations.

Result: Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, achieving MAE of 6.12 years and correlation of 0.880.

Conclusion: Overturns the conventional consensus that finger vein modality is limited for age estimation; previous failures were artifacts of biased public datasets.

Abstract: Age estimation from finger vein images has been widely considered impractical due to severe demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors like gender. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE-Vein, a novel multi-instance, multi-task learning framework. Our approach extracts robust structural aging signs by employing a hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers, effectively suppressing local imaging noise. Furthermore, simultaneous optimization of gender classification conditions the network to effectively eliminate gender-specific vascular variations. Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880. Our results not only overturn the conventional consensus regarding the limitations of the finger vein modality but also demonstrate that previous estimation failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsisaoki/MAGE-Vein.

</details>


### [22] [DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20900)
*Pierre Gallin-Martel,Mika Feng,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DINO-VPT is a lightweight, vision-only framework using hierarchical visual prompt tuning and a Prompt Routing Network (PRN) to unify physical and digital face anti-spoofing detection, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy without multimodal fusion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing VLM-based FAS methods achieve high generalization but rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. There is a need for a simpler, unified model that can handle both physical and digital spoofing attacks.

Method: Proposes DINO-VPT, a vision-only framework with hierarchical visual prompt tuning. It uses a Prompt Routing Network (PRN) to dynamically inject input-conditioned prompts into the model, enabling disentanglement of diverse spoofing artifacts without multimodal components.

Result: DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods on the UniAttackData benchmark.

Conclusion: A properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without requiring multimodal supervision or external text encoders.

Abstract: With the increasing diversity of spoofing attacks, there is a growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. While existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate high generalization in this context, they heavily rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. In this paper, we propose DINO-VPT, a lightweight, vision-only framework leveraging hierarchical visual prompt tuning. By dynamically injecting prompts conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), our method effectively disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without requiring multimodal fusion. Evaluations on the UniAttackData benchmark demonstrate that DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. Our results indicate that a properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without the need for multimodal supervision.

</details>


### [23] [Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20903)
*Liu Liu,Freya Huying Tan,Fábio Duarte*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Richer visual representations (video) don't always align better with human judgment of urban engagement; temporally averaged images (TAIs) match or outperform video in binary classification tasks, with video only superior in dynamic activity-driven scenes while TAIs excel in composition-driven static scenes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To test whether richer visual representations (e.g., full video) yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement compared to simpler representations (e.g., temporally averaged images, audio, text).

Method: Analyzed 61 first-person city-walk videos (50,000+ ten-second clips) across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, TAIs, audio embeddings, and text descriptions. Used Spearman correlation, binary classification across quantile thresholds, and a two-alternative forced-choice AMT study with gap analysis.

Result: Video features show strongest continuous alignment (temporal-richness continuum ordering), but under binary classification TAIs match or outperform video across most classifiers and thresholds. AMT study confirms human judgment parity between TAIs and video. Gap analysis reveals video advantages in activity-driven dynamic scenes, while TAIs align better in composition-driven static scenes.

Conclusion: Challenges the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned; perceptually grounded temporal compression (TAIs) can be a principled alternative to full video encoding for urban engagement measurement.

Abstract: We examine whether richer visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube segmented into over 50,000 ten-second clips and represented across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Spearman correlation analysis reveals the expected ordering along the temporal-richness continuum, with video features showing the strongest continuous alignment. However, this ordering breaks down under binary classification of high- versus low-engagement moments (the paradigm most commonly used to train perceptual scoring models), where TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. An independent two-alternative forced-choice study on Amazon Mechanical Turk confirms that this parity reflects human judgment: participants identified engaging moments with comparable accuracy from TAIs and full video clips, while text performed substantially worse and audio remained near chance. Gap analysis reveals a functional dissociation: video features are advantaged in activity-driven scenes with dynamic content, whereas TAIs better align with human judgments in composition-driven scenes dominated by stable spatial structure. These findings challenge the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned, and suggest that perceptually grounded temporal compression can be a principled alternative to full video encoding.

</details>


### [24] [FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20922)
*Yingdong Hu,Yisheng He,Yiming Jiang,Zehong Lin,Steven Hoi,Jun Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FA-LAM is a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation that addresses attention noise and task conflicts between reconstruction and animation via symmetric semantic attention regularization and dual-phase training, enabling high-quality static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Prior state-of-the-art approaches for animatable head avatars suffer from two key issues: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between reconstruction and animation tasks, which compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation.

Method: (1) Symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy leveraging inherent head semantics and structural symmetry. (2) Dual-phase training pipeline separating large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. (3) Core autoregressive modification with visibility-aware token fusion for efficient multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction.

Result: FA-LAM reconstructs animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, especially in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

Conclusion: The proposed innovations collectively enable high-quality one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation with both static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery capabilities.

Abstract: We propose FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery. The core of our method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches. Our analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation. To address the first issue, we introduce a symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy that leverages the inherent semantics and structural symmetry of human heads. To disentangle the objectives of reconstruction and animation, we develop a novel dual-phase training pipeline that separates the model's capabilities for large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. Moreover, we enhance our model to support multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction in an efficient and memory-friendly manner through a core autoregressive modification with tailored visibility-aware token fusion. Collectively, these innovations enable FA-LAM to reconstruct animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, particularly in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

</details>


### [25] [MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20924)
*Ziyi Wang,Siming Zheng,Yang Yang,Shusong Xu,Hao Zhang,Bo Li,Changqing Zou,Peng-Tao Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MagicMakeup is a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable, high-fidelity makeup transfer that addresses pixel-to-attention misalignment (via Token-Aligned Region Gating), concept coupling between makeup and identity (via Cross-Modal Perception Guidance), and the lack of high-resolution region-labeled datasets (via a 1024×1024 data generation pipeline).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing diffusion-based makeup transfer methods suffer from (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment causing makeup spillover to non-target regions, (ii) unclear separation between transfer and preservation concepts under two-image conditioning leading to identity-makeup coupling, and (iii) lack of high-resolution identity-consistent region-labeled datasets for fine-grained supervision.

Method: Proposes MagicMakeup built on a diffusion transformer with two key modules: (1) Token-Aligned Region Gating that aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating for precise regional editing, and (2) Cross-Modal Perception Guidance that aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception and disentangle makeup/identity. Also introduces a pipeline for generating 1024×1024 data pairs via region-specific makeup removal.

Result: Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate improved regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across diverse styles, races, and poses.

Conclusion: MagicMakeup effectively addresses key challenges in makeup transfer through spatial constraints and concept disentanglement, establishing a unified benchmark in both synthetic and real settings.

Abstract: Makeup-transfer applies the reference makeup to the source face while preserving the source identity. Despite advances in full-face editing by diffusion-based methods, strong regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation remain challenging. The reasons are (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment that causes spillover into non-target areas and weakens regional control; (ii) unclear transfer/preservation concept separation under two-image conditioning, leading to coupling between makeup attributes and identity; and (iii) the lack of a high-resolution dataset that is identity-consistent and region-labeled for fine-grained supervision. In this paper, we propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable and high-fidelity makeup transfer, built on spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. To enable precise region-specific editing while preserving identity, we propose Token-Aligned Region Gating, which aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating. To clarify the concepts of transfer and preservation, we further introduce Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, which aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception. We also design a pipeline for the generation of 1024 x 1024 data pairs through region-specific makeup removal and establish a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MagicMakeup improves regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

</details>


### [26] [Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20940)
*Zekun Li,Xiaoyan Cong,Hongyu Li,Zhiyang Dou,Chuan Guo,Abhay Mittal,Sizhe An,Srinath Sridhar*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Ms.Forcing is an efficient streaming video diffusion model that adapts spatial granularity to noise levels via Multi-Scale Patchification (reducing token count by 45%) and Multi-Scale Self-Attention, achieving 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU (39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing) with improved VBench scores.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Streaming video diffusion models suffer from slow real-time deployment due to nested autoregressive and denoising loops. Rolling-window methods improve throughput but waste computation by tokenizing all states at the same fine granularity regardless of noise level, leaving noise-dependent redundancy.

Method: Proposes Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) that assigns coarser patches to noisier states to reduce token count by 45%, and Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) that matches visible non-sink key/value density to query scale. Also introduces Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD) to reduce mismatch between training and inference sequences.

Result: Achieves 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, with significantly improved VBench scores for both short and long video generation.

Conclusion: Ms.Forcing demonstrates that adapting spatial granularity to noise levels improves efficiency and quality in streaming video generation, with a static computation graph friendly to hardware deployment.

Abstract: Streaming video diffusion models have made substantial progress toward interactive and dynamic world simulation, but the nested autoregressive and denoising loops of conventional next-frame generation hinder real-time deployment. Recent rolling-window methods pipeline denoising across multiple consecutive frames at different noise levels, improving throughput and long-horizon stability. However, they tokenize every state at the same fine spatial granularity, leaving substantial noise-dependent redundancy in the joint denoising window. We propose Ms.Forcing, an efficient streaming video generation paradigm that adapts spatial granularity to each state's noise level. Its Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier states, reducing the active-window token count by 45%, while Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches the density of visible non-sink keys and values to each query scale to further reduce attention cost. Because both schedules are fixed by window position, Ms.Forcing retains a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. We further introduce Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD), which assembles each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level, thereby reducing the mismatch between DMD training sequences and inference-time rollouts. The multi-scale design helps offset the additional training cost of backpropagating through overlapping windows. We include both quantitative and qualitative experiments to show that Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, while significantly improving VBench scores in both short video and long video generation setting.

</details>


### [27] [RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20947)
*Junsheng Du,Zhaocheng He,Yuhuan Lu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RECO is a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework for roadside 3D object detection that corrects camera extrinsics using piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets, partitioning scenes into near/far regions with learned boundaries and a differentiable sigmoid gate, achieving robust detection under extrinsic perturbations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing roadside 3D detection methods are highly sensitive to camera extrinsics; even slight deviations (jitter or drift) are amplified by projective geometry, causing severe feature misalignment and degraded localization.

Method: RECO predicts a learnable range boundary to partition the scene into near/far regions, estimates region-specific 6-DoF pose corrections, and uses a differentiable sigmoid gate to blend compensated geometries. An auxiliary reprojection loss comparing projected 2D boxes against annotations supervises extrinsic refinement jointly with the detection objective.

Result: Consistent improvements over SOTA baselines on DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under yaw and z-axis extrinsic perturbations, with generalization from transient jitter to persistent shifts under strict calibration uncertainty.

Conclusion: RECO effectively mitigates extrinsic sensitivity in roadside 3D detection through region-aware piecewise compensation and joint optimization with reprojection loss, maintaining robust performance across various perturbation types.

Abstract: In intelligent transportation systems, roadside 3D object detection provides wide-area perception crucial for traffic understanding, cooperative early warning, and safe autonomous driving. However, existing methods suffer from high sensitivity to camera extrinsics; even slight deviations (whether manifesting as transient jitter or persistent drift) can be significantly amplified by projective geometry. This cascade results in severe feature misalignment and degraded localization. To mitigate this limitation, we propose RECO, a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework that corrects extrinsics using piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets. RECO predicts a learnable range boundary to partition the scene into near and far regions, estimating region-specific pose corrections. A differentiable sigmoid gate then smoothly blends the two compensated geometries to preserve continuous BEV sampling and facilitate stable optimization. To supervise the refinement of extrinsics, we introduce an auxiliary reprojection loss that compares 2D bounding boxes projected from 3D ground truth against 2D annotations, optimizing it jointly with the standard detection objective. Extensive experiments on the DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under extrinsic perturbations demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across both yaw and $z$-axis deviations. RECO also generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent shifts, maintaining highly competitive performance under strict calibration uncertainty.

</details>


### [28] [FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20955)
*Linke Fan,Xianglong Li,Huixin Huang,Kai Shu*

Main category: cs.CV
